items.prompt: You are White. Black has just played 6...Nf6. Commit to a move before you open any hint.

claims.statement: Qb3 is the engine's first choice by a wide margin.

hints: Black's pieces are mostly at home, and the b7 pawn is undefended. Which of your pieces could attack it?
Your bishop on c4 already eyes f7. A queen move could pick up a second target at the same time.
Look for a queen move to the b-file.
items.explain: Qb3 attacks the b7 pawn while the bishop on c4 already eyes f7. At depth 16 the engine ranks it first, well above Be3 and Bg5, which only add a piece.

feedback_by_move.c1e3: A sound-looking developing move, but the engine rates it more than 100 centipawns below Qb3 at depth 16.
feedback_by_move.c1g5: It attacks the knight, but the engine rates it more than 100 centipawns below Qb3 at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black defended with 7...Qe7. You may win a pawn or keep developing. Commit to a move, then compare with the game.

claims.statement: Qxb7 and Nc3 are both engine-approved; Qxb7 is first by about 50 centipawns.

hints: Look at what is loose on the b-file, and at which of your pieces is still at home.
Two moves are strong here: one wins a pawn, one brings a piece out.
The pawn on b7 can be taken, or the b1 knight can come to c3.
items.explain: Both Qxb7 and Nc3 are strong: at depth 16 the engine puts Qxb7 about 50 centipawns above Nc3, and both far above the rest. In the game White played Nc3, developing a piece instead of taking the pawn.

feedback_by_move.e1g1: Castling develops too, but the engine rates it more than 100 centipawns below the two accepted moves at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black played 8...c6, defending b7. What do you play?

claims.statement: Bg5 is the engine's first choice.

hints: One of your minor pieces is still on its first rank.
Black's queen and knight stand on the same diagonal. Which bishop move uses that?
The bishop from c1 goes to the g-file.
items.explain: Bg5 attacks the knight on f6 with the queen standing behind it on e7. At depth 16 the engine ranks it first; Be3 develops too but is rated lower.

feedback_by_move.c1e3: A fine developing square, but at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 50 centipawns below Bg5.

items.prompt: Black played 9...b5, trying to drive the bishop away. Find White's reply. It may cost material.

claims.statement: Nxb5 is first by a wide margin at depth 16.

hints: Count Black's developed pieces, and count yours.
Black's king is still on e8, and the b-file and c-file are about to open.
A knight can capture on b5.
items.explain: Nxb5 gives a knight for a pawn, but at depth 16 the engine ranks it first, more than 250 centipawns ahead of the capture on f6. That is an engine fact about this position, not a general rule about sacrifices.

feedback_by_move.g5f6: Taking the knight keeps material level, but the engine rates it more than 250 centipawns below Nxb5 at depth 16.

items.prompt: After 10.Nxb5 cxb5 11.Bxb5+ Nbd7, what do you play? One piece of yours is still not in the fight.

claims.statement: O-O-O is the engine's first choice.

hints: Which of your pieces has not moved yet?
You want the king safe and a rook on the open file in one move.
items.explain: O-O-O brings the last rook to the d-file with the king safe. At depth 16 the engine ranks it first, more than 200 centipawns above the capture on f6.

feedback_by_move.g5f6: Capturing first lets Black untangle, and the engine rates it more than 200 centipawns below castling at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black has just played 15...Nxd7. White to move. Look at the black king and at what guards b8.

claims.statement: Qb8+ Nxb8 Rd8# is a forced mate in two.

hints: Black's king has no free squares nearby.
A check that the knight must capture can pull a defender away from d8.
items.explain: Qb8+ forces the knight to take the queen, and then Rd8 is mate. The mate in two is checked by the engine.
